title: T1565 — Data Manipulation
subtitle: The scenario is “Three attacks, one bank”.

nodes.label: Sensitive data
nodes.tip: Sensitive data - What is at risk

steps.title: The intruder lands on a server
steps.caption: Using a stolen VPN account, the attacker signs in from a new country and reaches a bank jump server, FIN-JUMP-01. A small backdoor service starts and waits for commands. The VPN allowed the login because the password was valid
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

fields.detail: Using a stolen VPN account, the attacker signs in from a new country and reaches a bank jump server,

detection.label: No detection
detection.detail: This activity is not visible to the victim yet.

steps.title: Stored data manipulation (T1565.001)
steps.caption: From the server, the attacker opens a database session and changes one customer balance record. The change is small, so it sits below alert thresholds. The database keeps serving traffic; nothing looks broken
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: The SOC sees the stored-data hits
steps.caption: Two signals arrive together: the database audit log shows an UPDATE on the accounts table at 02:14, outside any change window, and file integrity monitoring reports a checksum change on the SWIFT export folder. The analyst links both to the same server
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Transmitted data manipulation (T1565.002)
steps.caption: The attacker now touches data in motion. A payment message travels from the SWIFT software toward the gateway and the print path. The attacker alters fields on the way, so the printed instruction does not match the stored record
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: The SOC sees the transit anomalies
steps.caption: The print server reports an unknown module, and the proxy logs a TLS session with a new certificate on an internal path. Neither alert alone proves fraud, but both point at the same payment flow
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Runtime data manipulation (T1565.003)
steps.caption: On the review workstation, the attacker patches the PDF viewer in memory. When the reviewer opens the statement, the viewer hides the fraudulent rows. The disk file stays untouched, so file scans see nothing wrong
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Reviewer and EDR break the illusion
steps.caption: The endpoint platform raises a memory-tamper alert on the viewer process. At the same time, the reviewer compares the statement with the database and finds rows that do not match. The fraud is blocked before the money leaves the bank
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Response and integrity restore
steps.caption: The SOC opens a P1 case, isolates the server and the workstation, and revokes the stolen VPN account. The team restores the changed records from a trusted backup, verifies them against checksums, and reports the incident to the regulator
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.
